sections.overview: The Tonkin snub-nosed monkey is a leaf-eating monkey found only in northern Vietnam, and the only snub-nosed monkey of subtropical forests. It is Critically Endangered and has long been counted among the 25 most endangered primates in the world.
sections.identification: A fairly slender monkey with a body of 51–65 cm and a tail of 66–92 cm, longer than the body. Males average about 13.8 kg and females about 8.3 kg. The back, outer limbs, hands and feet are black, while the chest, elbows and inner limbs are creamy white. The nose is upturned and the skin around it and the eyes is bare and pale blue; the throat is orange, more strongly in males. Juveniles are greyish black.
sections.habitat: It lives in subtropical broad-leaf and bamboo evergreen forest with monsoon rains, usually on limestone hills below 1,000 m. It is confined to northern Vietnam and now survives in a few areas of karst limestone peaks, among them the Khau Ca conservation area.
sections.diet: It eats mainly leaves, especially bamboo and other evergreen leaves, but is not strictly a leaf-eater: fruit, flowers and seeds are also eaten. One study listed 31 food species from 21 plant families. Like other leaf-eating monkeys it has a stomach with several compartments and strong jaw muscles for tough plant food.
sections.behavior: It is active by day and lives in the trees, walking on all fours and also climbing and leaping. Groups are either all-male or made of one male with several females and young. Groups split and merge and the species does not appear to be territorial. It sleeps on lower branches near steep slopes, sheltered from cold night winds, and its main call is a hiccup-like sound used as alarm and contact.
sections.reproduction: The mating system is polygynous. Gestation lasts about 200 days and females give birth to one or two young in spring or summer. Females mature at about 4 years and males at about 7. The breeding season, the interval between births and the length of nursing have not been reported.
sections.ecology: As a plant-eater it may shape the vegetation around it, and the fruit it eats may help spread seeds. Humans are its only confirmed predator; snakes, large birds of prey and forest cats probably take some, but this has not been confirmed.
sections.conservation: It is considered Critically Endangered and is listed in CITES Appendix I. A 2025 census by Fauna & Flora counted about 160 animals in the Khau Ca conservation area, a stable population, and the total is estimated at about 250. Hunting for food and traditional medicine was once the key threat and is illegal; the main current threats are habitat loss and deforestation, notably for farmland, along with bamboo harvesting and gold mining.
